explanation: A good model has to fit the intended context, including edge cases and exceptions. If some requests are created before a customer exists, the original rule is too narrow and should be adjusted to reflect the real business situation.

options.text: The model may not fit an important exception in the intended business context.
The model uses too many entity types.
The model cannot be implemented in SQL.
The model should always treat every relationship as mandatory.

prompt: A team models customer support requests and first draws a simple rule that every request must be linked to exactly one customer. During review, they realize some requests are created by internal staff before a customer account exists. What is the best reason to revisit the model?
